Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Issue: Per-query parked-output bookkeeping in the CN. Three designs were written to /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-surgical.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-robust.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-upstream.md. Their structured summaries: [

  "summary": "Surgical fix for the CN's per-query parked-output bookkeeping (report finding B4, plan issue 2). One idea, three files, all in experimental/starrocks/src: the engine thread tags every ParkedOutput with its query_id, keeps a bounded failed-query memory, drops only the failed query's parked outputs on Err (the process-wide wipe survives only for unlabelled fixtures), skips any later Run of a failed query before touching the GPU, and exposes one fire-and-forget request AbandonQuery. Two CN call sites invoke it: run_ready_fragment's Err arm (covers the q16 translation-failure leak and every other pre-run failure) and cancel_plan_fragment gated to reasons other than QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH (the FE cancels every instance of every query, reason 5 or 1 on success, measured 642 cancels in cn1/cluster.log, so the gate is what keeps the 15 passing queries untouched). local_exchange.rs, result_store.rs, nixl_transport.rs, engine C++ and FE are untouched. Full design with code excerpts and file:line citations: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-surgical.md",
  "mechanism": "engine.rs: (a) ParkedOutput gains query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId> copied from request.label.query_id at park time (engine.rs:710-716). (b) A FailedQueries map (id -> first cause, FIFO-capped at 1024) lives on the engine thread next to parked/parked_slots/poisoned (engine.rs:267-275). (c) In the Run arm (engine.rs:282-318) a Run whose label.query_id is in FailedQueries is answered Err(\"fragment of query .. skipped: the query already failed on this CN: <cause>\") before context.fragment()/build()/GPU work. (d) The Err arm's wipe body (engine.rs:301-315) becomes abandon_query(parked, parked_slots, poisoned, failed_queries, request.label.query_id, err): retain parked entries of other queries, poison only the dropped slots (poisoned.clear() first, today's bound), record the failure; query_id None keeps today's process-wide wipe. (e) New EngineRequest::AbandonQuery{query_id,cause} with no respond channel (must never wait behind a running fragment, same rule as the staging bypass at engine.rs:16-21); handler = abandon_query. FIFO on the existing channel: a Run queued before it runs and parks then is dropped, a Run queued after is skipped. fragment_executor.rs: trait method abandon_query(query_id, cause) -> Result<(), String>, default Ok(()) (a stub parks nothing); SiriusEngine sends without receiving. compute_node_service.rs: (f) run_ready_fragment Err arm (:877-897) calls executor.abandon_query(query_id, error) after results.fail_query, covering translation failure (:1361), output-name mismatch (:1347), sink validation (:1066-1131), drain failure (:872); (g) cancel_plan_fragment (:457-479) keeps results.cancel and additionally calls abandon_query when request.query_id is Some and cancel_reason is not QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH (proto internal_service.proto:464-482; FE DefaultCoordinator.java:1028-1034 success reasons, :764-786 failure reasons, :1161-1167 error_message only for INTERNAL_ERROR). Measured cases: q05: 5774's Err records q05 and drops its 2 slots; the worker's later Runs 5773/5777/5776 and receiver 5775 (which today relayed 11 batches and parked 4.69 GB, cluster.log 6072-6305) are skipped; q06's first fragment starts ~0.72 s earlier at allocated=0. q16: senders ff87/ff86 parked 6.6 GB, receiver ff85 failed translation on the worker (cluster.log 16593) -> abandon_query drops both. q21->q22: leftovers acc (179 ms) and acb (3153 ms, 36.64 GB) skipped. Passing queries: one HashMap::get on an empty map per Run, no Err path taken, cancels with reason 5/1 take the unchanged path; no added engine message, no ordering or determinism change. Sync dispatch mode (default off): Runs already queued on the engine channel at failure time still run and park, then the AbandonQuery that follows drops them; the campaign ran with async dispatch (capture-cn.sh:12) where nothing is queued ahead. Explicit non-goals: LocalExchange removal by query (stale PendingReceiver is host-side KBs; a readied receiver of a dead query is skipped anyway), aborting a running fragment (fix 1), ResultStore changes.",

  "predicted_effect": "Measured leaks removed: 4.69 (q05->q06/q07), 8.83 (q08->q09), 31.56 (q09->q10..q16), +6.60 (q16->q17), 4.00 (q17->q18), 36.64 (q21->q22) GB all become 0 (engine-cn0.log [gpu_pool] QueryBegin allocated returns to 0 after each failure). Headroom for q07 (own peak 79.17 GB) 23.51 -> 28.2 GB; q07 placed between q09 and q17 would fit instead of the inferred 110.7 GB OOM (order-independence restored). q10-q16 and q22 timings taken with a clean pool instead of 31.6/36.6 GB occupied; C3's 47-178 ms reservation-gate blocks in q10/q12/q14 may shrink, otherwise within noise (oom_resched=0 already). Inference except where marked measured in the design.",

  "summary": "Replace the CN's process-wide parked-output wipe with one query-scoped teardown, ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause), reachable from three triggers (a fragment failure on the engine or CN side, an FE cancel_plan_fragment, a TTL sweep) and acting on four subsystems: a new ParkedRegistry<F> on the engine thread (keyed by query, drops only that query's fragments, tolerates the transport's late drop_parked), two run gates (dispatch worker/run_labeled and engine dequeue+park) that refuse fragments of a dead query, LocalExchange::remove_query/remove_receiver_instance (purges rendezvous state and releases staged remote leases), and the result store (fail_query on INTERNAL_ERROR, release-only on QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH). Idempotent, non-blocking cancel handler, one structured 'query teardown' log line per trigger, two knobs. Design written to /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-robust.md.",
  "mechanism": "Measured today (cn1/cluster.log, headroom.txt): after each of the six failures the engine Err path wipes every parked slot (engine.rs:291-316), then the dead query's queued senders still run on the engine thread (dispatch_worker compute_node_service.rs:380-390 and run_ready_fragment :864-909 have no notion of a dead query) and park 0-36.64 GB nobody consumes (q05 4.69, q08 8.83, q09 31.56, q16 +6.60, q17 4.00, q21 36.64 GB; 0.72/1.04/0.39/6.42/3.35 s of engine time stolen); q16's translation failure never reaches the engine so its 6.6 GB of parked inputs is never dropped; cancel_plan_fragment (:457-482) only marks the result store, and the FE's first cancel arrives 0.25 ms AFTER the next leftover sender started, so Err-time bookkeeping on the CN is mandatory and cancel is the second line. On 1 CN the wipe itself was not the leak (only the failing query's slots were parked); the leftover runs are. Design: (1) engine.rs maps -> ParkedRegistry<F> in parked.rs with ParkedOutput{query_id,...}, torn_down map replacing `poisoned`, drop_query(query)->DropReport, release() returning Ok(AlreadyTornDown) for torn-down slots (transport's post-eos drop_parked stays correct), get_mut() -> Err naming the teardown cause; a shared Arc<Mutex<HashMap<QueryId,cause>>> `terminated` checked at Run dequeue (GATE 1) and again before park (GATE 2, drops output of a fragment whose query died mid-run); Err marks the query on the engine thread itself. (2) FragmentExecutor::terminate_query(query_id, cause) non-blocking: inserts into `terminated`, posts EngineRequest::DropQuery without waiting (never blocks behind a running fragment). (3) ServiceCore.lifecycle map; terminate_query called from run_ready_fragment's Err arm (covers engine failures, translation failures with slots in hand, drain failures), from inline RPC Err in process_fragment, and from cancel_plan_fragment by reason (3/4/2 -> Cancelled + fail_query_all with the FE's message; 5/1 -> Finished, release-only; finst_id (0,0) query-level; missing query_id -> today's behaviour + instance purge). Dispatch gates in run_ready_fragment and run_labeled skip fragments of terminated queries and log 'skipping fragment of a terminated query'. (4) LocalExchange records receiver->query at register_receiver/push_sender; remove_query and remove_receiver_instance return purged SenderSources so staged remote batches' leases are staging_release'd. (5) TTL sweep on the engine thread (SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS default 1800, warn at half) for an FE that never cancels; retention of terminated/torn_down 600 s. FE facts verified: BackendServiceClient.java:192-209 always sets query_id, error_message only for INTERNAL_ERROR; DefaultCoordinator.java:1003-1035/1161-1177 cancels every deployed instance on failure (INTERNAL_ERROR) and on eos (QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH).",

  "tests": [

  "predicted_effect": "1-CN SF1000 sweep in campaign order: the seven post-failure leaks (4.69, 8.83, 31.56, +6.60, 4.00, 0, 36.64 GB) become 0; the 11.9 s of engine-thread time spent on dead queries' fragments (q05->q06 0.72, q08->q09 1.04, q09->q10 0.39, q17->q18 6.42, q21->q22 3.35 s) disappears; q22 cold 4110 -> ~1000-1200 ms (own fragments 755 ms + ~200 ms FE head), q06 cold 2453 -> ~1750-1950 ms, q18 time-to-first-fragment 6.42 s -> <0.3 s; q10-q16 and q22 warm timings become valid on a clean pool and the 47-178 ms reservation-gate blocks in q10/q12/q14 (tied to the 31.6 GB leak in C3) are predicted to vanish (inference, up to ~0.18 s per run); order independence restored (q07's 79.17 GB + 31.56 GB leak would exceed the 107.37 GB cap, inference).   "risks": [
   "Cancel contract drift: assumes StarRocks sends QUERY_FINISHED only after the FE holds every row (DefaultCoordinator.java:1022-1035); mitigated by release-only semantics, the AlreadyTornDown idempotency, the 4-CN smoke assertion slots=0, and the SIRIUS_CN_TEARDOWN_ON_CANCEL escape hatch",
   "GATE 2 discards the output of a fragment that finished after its query was terminated; a mis-marked query would lose live output loudly ('terminated while running') - first-cause-wins and the cause text keep it diagnosable",
   "TTL misconfiguration can expire a legitimately long query's parked output (default 1800 s = 6x FE query_timeout; warn at half; 0 disables)",
   "Engine cannot abort a running fragment: a cancel during a 100 s fragment of the same query releases memory only when it ends (fix 1/B3 territory); DropQuery is FIFO behind the running fragment",
   "Refusing a late deploy of a terminated query returns an RPC error to an FE that already failed the query (harmless); retention 600 s must exceed the deploy window",
   "Interaction with fix 4(b): if parked repositories are registered with the downgrade executor, Fragment drop must unregister them; output_row_count throws on spilled batches so DropReport.rows stays optional",
   "Behavioural change on the inline sender path: queued senders of a dead query now return an RPC error instead of running; the FE already treats the query as failed",
   "Two terminated maps (engine-owned and ServiceCore-owned) fed from one entry point; kept separate so FragmentExecutor remains the test seam - a missed call site would desynchronise them (covered by the component tests)"

- ooc-sort-dev: Use when developing, building, testing, or iterating on the disk-backed (out-of-core) sort implementation for cudf-polars in ~/bzaitlen/test-data/ooc-sort/. Covers installing into the rapidsmpf container env, running streaming sort tests, and the phase-by-phase implementation workflow.
- build-errors: Use this skill when the build fails, compilation errors occur, or you see undefined references, linker errors, CUDA compilation issues, missing headers, or template instantiation failures. Analyzes errors, suggests fixes, and iteratively rebuilds until success.
- build-sirius-starrocks: Build the Sirius-as-StarRocks-CN stack on a fresh GPU box — UCX, nixl, libsirius, StarRocks FE, and the Rust CN. Use when standing the stack up from scratch, recovering a broken toolchain (g++/ld/nvml shims, CUDA 13, no-root conda deps), applying the StarRocks proto patch, or relocating pixi/cargo/Maven onto local NVMe.
- cn-tuning: Size Sirius StarRocks CN memory and operator budgets for a given GPU box and TPC-H scale factor. Use when choosing GPU_MEM, STAGING, HOST_MEM, hash_partition_bytes, scan_task_batch_size, or when a query OOMs / exhausts the exchange arena / looks like an engine bug that is actually mis-sizing. Covers the derived-flag path vs a full sirius.yaml.
- dataset-manager: Use this skill to generate benchmark datasets (TPC-H, TPC-DS, etc.). Trigger when the user needs test data at a specific scale factor for benchmarking or testing. Supports parquet and duckdb output formats.
- log-analyzer: Use this skill to analyze Sirius query execution logs — to find why a query is slow, diagnose validation errors (wrong results), spot excessive downgrading, identify pipeline gaps, or compare two runs of the same query. Trigger whenever the user mentions a Sirius log file, says "look at this log", asks about per-operator time, pipeline gaps, memory pressure, downgrade behavior, validation/correctness mismatches, or wants to compare two query runs. Also use as a hand-off target from race-check (for two-run comparisons), runtime-errors (for "where did the query stall before hang"), and validate (for diffing the bad run against a good run). This is the log-only counterpart to profile-analyzer (nsys) and optimization-advisor (source-level guidance).
- module-context: Automatically identify which dependency library modules are relevant to a task and load their API documentation into context. Use PROACTIVELY before implementing features, fixing bugs, or writing new operators — analyzes the task description and loads cudf, rmm, duckdb, cucascade module docs to improve code quality. Trigger when the user asks to implement, add, fix, or modify GPU operators, pipeline components, memory management, joins, aggregations, sorting, expressions, or data I/O.
- module-discover: Discover and document a dependency library or submodule — analyzes all uses within the codebase, divides the library into logical modules, identifies which modules are used, and generates LLM-consumable API documentation for each module. Use when the user wants to understand a library dependency, map its modules, or generate API reference docs for a submodule.
- optimization-advisor: Use this skill to find exactly which source code to optimize for better GPU performance. Maps nsys profile hotspots to specific Sirius source files and functions, classifies bottlenecks as GPU-bound, CPU-bound, or sync-bound, and recommends actionable code changes. Trigger when the user wants to know what to optimize, where to focus coding effort, or wants source-level optimization guidance. This skill focuses on actionable source code targets — for generating performance reports and measurements, use profile-analyzer instead.
- pr-digest: Generates a "learning" PR-review digest — a markdown file at PR_digests/PR_digest_<N>.md that explains what a GitHub PR does, why, and exactly where in the code, with clickable file/line links and trimmed diffs. Use this whenever the user shares a GitHub PR URL (e.g. github.com/owner/repo/pull/1234) and wants to understand, summarize, review, walk through, or get up to speed on what changed — phrases like "can you review this PR", "what does this PR do", "help me understand this pull request", "summarize the changes in PR
- pre-commit-cleanup: Clean the current Git changes before committing. Use when preparing to commit or when the pre-commit cleanliness hook blocks a commit.
- profile-analyzer: Use this skill to understand why a Sirius query is slow, identify GPU bottlenecks, or detect performance regressions. Generates reports with kernel occupancy, memory bandwidth, operator attribution, and cross-run comparisons. Trigger when the user mentions profiling, nsys, GPU utilization, kernel analysis, performance reports, or wants to compare query timings across runs. This skill focuses on measurement and reporting — for mapping hotspots to source code fixes, use optimization-advisor instead.

content.content:
1	# Plan: best solutions for the four SF1000 blockers, and the workflows that deliver them
2	
3	Written 2026-09-03 15:20 UTC from the report `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md`
4	(sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/` (indexed by `WORKFLOW-PLAN.md` there).
5	Working tree for all code: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-*` worktrees of the sirius-stacks clone,
6	one branch per fix off `perf/profile-sf1000` (45dab3be = d24f02c4 + aggregate gate + async dispatch + Quent probes).
7	Never the shared clone `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius`. No pushes, no PRs until asked.
8	
9	## The four issues
10	
11	| # | issue | where it lives | measured cost today (SF1000, 1 CN, 100 GiB pool) |
12	|---|---|---|---|
13	| 1 | The OOM reschedule loop has no feasibility check | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp` (:263 reservation gate, :330-420 reschedule, MAX_RETRIES=100, 50 ms sleep) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 take 54-232 s to die (775 s of a 910 s sweep); 17,917 "0 bytes freed, proceeding with partial reservation" lines |
14	| 2 | No per-query parked-output bookkeeping | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs` (:291-316 process-wide wipe on Err), `compute_node_service.rs` (:449-476 cancel is result-store only), `local_exchange.rs` (removals only in take_ready) | 0-38 GB of a dead query's parked output survives into later queries; dead query's queued senders still run (q22 cold 4110 vs 943 ms) |
15	| 3 | The FE plans every FILES() scan at 1 row | StarRocks FE `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (:664-676), `TableFunctionTable.java` (file sizes at :611, schema RPC), `PGetFileSchemaResult` (proto :647-650), CN `file_schema.rs` | every distribution decision is data-blind: 1 CN broadcasts 3.79B lineitem rows into q04's semi join, 4 CNs shuffle 3.23B rows for q03; all six failures are one plan shape |
16	| 4 | Six queries cannot run on 1 CN | fragment cut (FE) + receiver-first full materialisation (`engine.rs` run_fragment_inner, `local_exchange.rs`) + parked repositories outside the downgrade sweep (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300`) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 OOM; standalone Sirius runs them in 2.7-6.5 s |
17	
18	## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)
19	
20	1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
21	2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
22	3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
23	4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.
24	
25	## Evaluation criteria (judges score 1-5 each)
26	
27	1. Does it fix the measured failure at SF1000 on this box (which queries, predicted numbers, how verified)?
28	2. Correctness risk and blast radius (which paths change for the 15 passing queries; determinism; cancellation).
29	3. Size and reviewability as an upstream PR (target layer in the carve plan: engine `src/` -> dev PR; CN `experimental/starrocks` -> fork PR; FE -> checked-in patch), tests it needs.
30	4. Effort and dependencies (what must land first; FE rebuild; proto change).
31	5. Measurability: an acceptance test that a reviewer can rerun in minutes plus the SF1000 arm.
32	
33	## Acceptance tests (must exist before implementation is "done")
34	
35	| fix | unit / component test | SF1000 verification (orchestrator-run, one arm at a time) |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| 1 | Catch2 test in `test/cpp/pipeline/` driving a task through the reschedule path with a memory space that never frees: query fails within a bounded number of attempts with the new error text; contention case still retries | 1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21: time-to-fail <= 5 s each (was 54-232 s), error names parked bytes; the 15 passing queries unchanged (warm medians within noise, `compare.py` set unchanged) |
38	| 2 | Rust tests in `engine.rs`/`local_exchange.rs`/`compute_node_service.rs`: failure drops only that query's slots; queued senders of a failed query are skipped; cancel drops parked outputs; translation failure drops slots in hand | 1 CN sweep in the same order as before: `[gpu_pool] allocated` returns to baseline after each failure (was +4.7..+38 GB), q22 cold no longer inflated, no `fragment run started` for a dead query after its failure |
39	| 3 | FE unit test (Java) for the new statistics path; CN test if the proto changes; `EXPLAIN COSTS` golden outputs for q03 q04 q05 q22 at 1 and 4 CNs showing real cardinalities and the new join sides | 1 CN and 4 CN sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six: plan shapes recorded, timings vs the campaign table, oracle compares |
40	| 4 | Fusion: translator/CN tests that a single-destination local exchange fuses and the fused plan matches the sender+receiver plan; spill: Catch2 test that a parked repository is swept to HOST and relayed back | 1 CN: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass with oracle MATCH; report their times against standalone (2.7-6.5 s) |
41	
42	## Workflows
43	
44	**A. Design exploration (`fix/design-workflow.js`).** Per issue, three independent designers with different angles (surgical minimum, robust design, what upstream would accept), each reads the report finding, the evidence and the code and returns a design (mechanism, files, tests, risks, predicted effect). Two judges per issue score the three against the criteria and pick or merge. One synthesizer per issue writes the spec `scratchpad/fix/designs/<issue>-SPEC.md`. A final integrator checks the four specs for interactions (fail-fast vs bookkeeping ordering; fusion vs spill vs cardinalities) and writes the build order.
45	
46	**B. Implementation (`fix/implement-workflow.js`).** Per issue in its own worktree: implementer (tests first, then code, build, run the unit tests; commits with Conventional Commits and the Claude trailer), adversarial reviewer, fixer, verifier (fresh build + tests + clippy/fmt/pre-commit). Agents never start clusters or use GPUs other than the one assigned to their worktree (fix 1: GPU 0, fix 2: GPU 1, fix 3: none, fix 4: GPU 2). The orchestrator then runs the SF1000 arms from the table above, one at a time, and an integration branch with all four for the final sweep.
47	
48	**C. Report.** `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-top4-fixes-report.md`: per fix, what changed, tests, SF1000 before/after, what is left; plus the PR plan (branch, base, size) for when pushing is asked for.
49	
50	## Status log
51	- 15:20 UTC: worktrees `fix-oom-failfast`, `fix-parked-bookkeeping`, `fix-files-cardinality`, `fix-fragment-fusion` being created and built; design workflow launched.

# Fix 2, robust design: query-scoped teardown of parked output on the CN

Angle: the design a senior engineer ships for the long run. Correct under cancellation and
concurrent queries, observable, configurable where it must be, with the failure modes written
down. Source tree read at `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` (branch
`perf/profile-sf1000`, 45dab3be); evidence at `scratchpad/perf/sf1000`. Every number is
**measured** (file named) or marked **inference**.

## 0. Summary

Today a query's parked sender output on a CN is released only by the receiver that consumes it.
When the query dies, three things go wrong (all measured on the 1-CN SF1000 sweep):

1. The engine thread's `Err` path wipes **every** parked output process-wide
   (`engine.rs:291-316`), which is collateral damage for any concurrent query and does not even
   help the failing one on 1 CN (see 4.1).
2. The dead query's not-yet-run senders keep running and park output nobody will consume
   (`dispatch_worker` has no notion of a dead query, `compute_node_service.rs:380-390`):
   0-36.64 GB leaked per failure, 0.39-6.42 s of engine-thread time stolen from the next query.
3. `cancel_plan_fragment` touches only the result store (`compute_node_service.rs:449-476`), and
   a failure that never enters the engine (translation, q16) drops nothing.

The design replaces the process-wide wipe with **one query-scoped teardown**,
`ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause)`, reachable from three triggers (a fragment
failure, an FE cancel, a TTL sweep) and acting on four subsystems (the engine's parked
registry, the dispatch path, the exchange rendezvous, the result store). Teardown is idempotent,
tolerates the transport's late `drop_parked`, refuses late `Run`s of the dead query at two gates,
logs one structured report per teardown, and has two knobs. It changes nothing on the hot path of
a healthy query beyond a hash lookup per fragment run.

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +

Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)

- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## Facts added after the 1-CN sweep (13:19 UTC)
5. Supported on the CN path at SF1000 (1 CN, 100 GiB pool): q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 pass (15). Fail: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 = OOM at GPU_SCAN after 100 reschedules
   (101 s, 168 s, 232 s, 104 s, 54 s, 114 s to die; 2500-5600 reschedule warnings each, see cn1-cnlog.txt); q16 = translator gap ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does not model").
6. q15 returned 0 rows in run 1 and 1 row in runs 0 and 2 on 1 CN: streams 18 and 22 (the revenue = max(revenue) join output) carried 0 rows in run 1 while every other stream was identical.
   The build has the canonical float-sum sort gated OFF (SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS unset), so the two independently computed FP64 sums can differ in the last bits. Follow-up arms cn1-canon-q15 / cn1-nocanon-q15 test this.
7. Engine executor pools default to pipeline num_threads: 4 (docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94); Quent "Queued" time per fragment is the wait for one of those slots plus the memory reservation gate.
   1-CN q04: scan fragment 37 tasks, Queued sum 19.9 s vs Computing 4.7 s inside a 1.2 s wall; join fragment requested 253 GB of reservations for a 61 GB summed peak (4x over-estimate).
8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".
9. FE plans with 4 CNs alive are in survey/explain4/ (plan-summary-4cn.txt); diff against plan-summary.txt shows whether node count changes any distribution decision.
10. Plan-node enum decode for the dumps (TPlanNodeType(N)): survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt (4 HASH_JOIN, 6 AGGREGATION, 8 SORT, 9 EXCHANGE, 17 FILE_SCAN, 28 PROJECT, ...).
11. The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. The FE's fragment cut (what is broadcast/shuffled) is fixed before any of this.
12. The FE's plan DEPENDS on the number of alive CNs even with cardinality 1 everywhere: with 4 CNs most joins flip from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED (shuffle) and fragment counts rise (q02 13->16, q08 11->16, q09 9->12; q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q04/q12/q14/q19 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q15 -> BUCKET_SHUFFLE). survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) vs survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt (4 CNs); card-compare-cn4.txt uses the 4-CN plans (q03 exch2 = 3.23B lineitem rows shuffled, q12 exch1 = 1.5B orders rows shuffled).

Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).
14. Standalone (one GPU, 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics) runs the same 15 queries; standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt holds its plans. 1-CN vs standalone warm medians (ms): q01 5073/4882, q02 1246/571, q03 3106/3050, q07 3476/3266, q11 970/336, q15 4685/2627, q20 4171/3023, q22 943/496 (results.md).
15. Pre-digested tables added: reservation-ratio.txt (per run: tasks, summed reservation request vs summed measured peak, ratio, summed Queued and Computing seconds, wall; cn1 q11 54x, q14 15x, q03 14x, q10 6x over-reservation), cn4-transmits.txt (nixl transmits per run: count, GB, elapsed/lease/write ms, write GB/s).

CN arms: q02 q04 q06 q12 q13 q14 q20 q22 MATCH; q01 q07 q19 differ by 9.6e-4 and q03 by 1.8e-3 in revenue sums (the known `1 - 0.07` FP64->DECIMAL(16,2) truncation from #1236's lowering, not a multi-CN defect); q10 differs with maxreldiff 12.3 over 48 cells of its 20 rows, most likely the same truncated revenue sums reordering the TOP-20 (verify by comparing the customer sets and the revenue column); q15 differs by 1.1e-3 on its single row and is also flaky in row count (see fact 6); q11 shows EMPTY because the query returns 0 rows at SF1000 on both engines (the bench kit does not scale q11's 0.0001 fraction by 1/SF), so it is not a defect but the compare cannot confirm it.

The CN path died on the same queries after 54-232 s of OOM reschedules. This is the central planning + backpressure contrast of the campaign.

1	# Fix 2, surgical variant: per-query parked-output bookkeeping in the CN
2	
3	Angle: the smallest change that removes the measured leak and the measured stolen engine time, with
4	provably zero behaviour change for the 15 passing queries. Everything lives in the CN crate
5	(`experimental/starrocks/src`), nothing in the engine C++, the FE, `local_exchange.rs` or
6	`result_store.rs`.
7	
8	Source tree read: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` at `45dab3be` (all `file:line` below
9	are from it). Evidence root: `scratchpad/perf/sf1000`. "Measured" = copied from a named evidence file;
10	"inference" is marked.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 1. The defect, restated from the evidence
15	
16	### 1.1 What the code does today (verified)
17	
18	1. The engine thread serves one request at a time (`engine.rs:278-280`). When a `Run` returns `Err` it
19	   wipes **every** parked sender output on the CN and poisons every slot with the error
20	   (`engine.rs:291-316`). Nothing remembers that the query failed: the next `Run` of the same query
21	   is executed normally.
22	2. `cancel_plan_fragment` only flips a `Waiting` result entry to `Failed`
23	   (`compute_node_service.rs:457-479`, `result_store.rs:205-212`). No engine call, no parked drop.
24	3. `run_ready_fragment` (dispatch worker) on `Err` calls `results.fail_query` and returns
25	   (`compute_node_service.rs:864-911`). `execute_ready_fragment` translates **before** it extracts
26	   the `LocalParked` slots (`:1361` then `:1365-1392`); a translation failure returns with those
27	   slots still parked in the engine and never referenced again.
28	4. `ResultStore.query_failures` is recorded (`result_store.rs:98`, `:174-179`) but only consulted by
29	   `reserve` (`:127`); no sender path reads it.
30	
31	### 1.2 What the FE sends (verified, code + log)
32	
33	- The FE cancels **every** fragment instance of **every** query, including successful ones:
34	  `DefaultCoordinator.java:1028-1034` sends `LIMIT_REACH` (1) when a LIMIT was satisfied, else
35	  `QUERY_FINISHED` (5); on a failure `handleErrorExecution` sends `INTERNAL_ERROR` (3) or `TIMEOUT`
36	  (4) (`:764-786`), and `cancelRemoteFragmentsAsync` attaches `queryStatus.getErrorMsg()` only for
37	  `INTERNAL_ERROR` (`:1161-1167`). Per instance: `FragmentInstanceExecState.java:383-415` passes
38	  `query_id`, `instanceId`, `cancelReason`, `errorMessage`. Proto: `internal_service.proto:464-482`.
39	- Measured in `cn1/cluster.log`: 642 `cancel_plan_fragment` lines for 66 runs. q01 gets 3 cancels
40	  with `cancel_reason=5` (lines 1131-1136), q02 13 cancels with `cancel_reason=1` (1934-1959);
41	  q05's 11 cancels carry `cancel_reason=3 error_message=Some("fragment instance ... failed: ...")`
42	  (6073-6094); q16's 5 cancels likewise (16597-16605); q21's 9 (21350-21367).
43	
44	  Consequence for the design: any cancel-path change must be gated on the reason, or it runs on
45	  every passing query.
46	
47	### 1.3 What happens after a failure (measured)
48	
49	q05, `cn1/cluster.log` (ANSI stripped, times UTC):
50	
51	| time | line | event |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| 13:05:24.626889 | 6050 | `discarding every parked sender output on this CN after a fragment failure slots=2` |
54	| 13:05:24.627064 | 6051 | `fragment run failed ... 5774 role="sender" elapsed_ms=101193` (lineitem, OOM at GPU_SCAN) |
55	| 13:05:24.632012 | 6072 | `fragment run started ... 5773` (dead query, 0.25 ms before the first cancel) |
56	| 13:05:24.632266-.633083 | 6073-6094 | 11 x `cancel_plan_fragment ... cancel_reason=3` |
57	| 13:05:24.640784 | 6097 | 5773 finished, 8 ms |
58	| 13:05:24.650830-.684200 | 6181-6237 | 5777 ran, 33 ms |
59	| 13:05:24.696997-25.279686 | 6258-6275 | 5776 ran, 582 ms |
60	| 13:05:25.282255-25.355984 | 6291-6305 | 5775 (receiver, `inputs=2`) declared streams 1 and 4 (150,000,000 and 227,571,151 rows), relayed 1 + 10 batches, ran 73 ms and parked its output for a receiver that never runs |
61	| 13:05:25.372453 | 6329 | q06's first fragment starts; the q06 client started 13:05:24.652 (`cn1/runs/runs.csv`) = 0.72 s stolen |
62	
63	Pool (`cn1/engine-cn0.log` 61738-61889): `QueryEnd q=219 allocated=104297693440` -> `QueryBegin
64	q=221 allocated=0` (the wipe) -> after 5773/5777/5776/5775: `allocated=4690817280` = **4.69 GB**
65	that q06 and q07 then ran under (`agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt` base@start).
66	
67	q21 -> q22 (`cluster.log` 21344-21617): failed 13:18:07.593; leftover `acc` ran 179 ms, `acb`
68	(`inputs=1`, relayed 8 batches = 730,806,711 rows of stream 6) ran **3153 ms** and parked; q22's first
69	fragment started 13:18:10.961 against a client start of 13:18:07.610: **3.35 s stolen, 36.64 GB
70	parked** into q22 (cold 4110 ms vs warm 971/915).
71	
72	q16 (`cluster.log` 16571-16605): senders `ff87` (partsupp, 108 ms) and `ff86` (25 ms) parked, then
73	the receiver `ff85` failed **translation** on the dispatch worker
74	(`dispatched intermediate receiver fragment failed ... malformed plan: two-phase aggregation ...`).
75	No `Run` returned `Err`, so no wipe: **+6.60 GB** (31.56 -> 38.16 GB, headroom.txt) that q17 started under.
76	
77	All six failures (`headroom.txt` base@start of the next run): q05 -> 4.69, q08 -> 8.83, q09 -> 31.56
78	(carried through q10..q16), q16 -> +6.60, q17 -> 4.00, q18 -> 0, q21 -> 36.64 GB. Stolen engine
79	time (`refute-oom5/notes.md`): q05->q06 0.72 s, q08->q09 1.04, q09->q10 0.39, q17->q18 6.42,
80	q21->q22 3.35 = **11.9 s**.
81	
82	Not caused by the leak (both skeptics, `refute-oom5/notes.md`): no pass/fail flipped; every failing
83	sender exceeds the 107.37 GB cap on its own. The leak only moved where q17 died (25 vs ~40 batches).
84	Order dependence is inference: q07's own peak 79.17 GB + 31.56 GB leak = 110.7 > 107.37.
85	
86	### 1.4 What the 15 passing queries do (measured)
87	
88	`cn1-cnlog.txt`: `fail=0` for all 45 passing runs; cancels are reason 5 or 1 only; the engine
89	`Err` arm never executed for them; `parked_slots` is empty at every query boundary
90	(`pool-trace.txt`: alloc returns to the pre-query baseline after each result fragment).
91	
92	---
93	
94	## 2. Mechanism
95	
96	One idea: **the engine thread remembers which queries failed and owns "abandon query" as a
97	primitive**; the two CN call sites that learn about a failure (the dispatch worker's `Err` arm and
98	the FE's non-success cancel) invoke that primitive. Everything else follows from FIFO ordering on
99	the existing engine channel.
100	
101	### 2.1 `engine.rs`
102	
103	**(a) Tag parked output with its query.** `ParkedOutput` (`engine.rs:44-47`) gains
104	`query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>`, copied from `request.label.query_id` at park time
105	(`engine.rs:710-716`). `FragmentLabel.query_id` is already carried on every `ExecuteRequest`
106	(`engine.rs:72`, `fragment_executor.rs:58-63`) and set by `fragment_label` for every FE-dispatched
107	fragment (`compute_node_service.rs:1584-1589`).
108	
109	**(b) A failed-query memory on the engine thread.** Next to `parked` / `parked_slots` / `poisoned`
110	(`engine.rs:267-275`), a `FailedQueries` value: `HashMap<FragmentInstanceId, String>` (id -> first
111	cause) plus a `VecDeque` for FIFO eviction at 1024 entries. Query ids are 128-bit unique, so a stale
112	entry can only ever match a fragment of the query that failed, and an evicted entry can only matter
113	if a fragment of a query that failed 1024 failures ago is still pending, which the FE's 300 s query
114	timeout rules out.
115	
116	**(c) Skip pending runs of a failed query.** In the `Run` arm (`engine.rs:282-318`), before
117	`run_fragment`:
118	
119	```rust
120	if let Some(query_id) = request.label.query_id
121	    && let Some(cause) = failed_queries.get(&query_id)
122	{
123	    let _ = request.respond.send(Err(format!(
124	        "fragment of query {query_id} skipped: the query already failed on this CN: {cause}"
125	    )));
126	    continue;
127	}
128	```
129	
130	No `context.fragment()`, no `build()`, no GPU work, no park. The error text carries the original
131	cause, so a result fragment skipped this way still names the real failure through `fetch_data`
132	(and `ResultStore::fail_query` keeps the first cause anyway, `result_store.rs:174-179`).
133	
134	**(d) Drop only the failed query's parked output.** Replace the body of the `Err` arm
135	(`engine.rs:301-315`) with a call to one function that both the `Err` arm and the new request use:
136	
137	```rust
138	/// Drops every parked output of `query_id` (all of them when the failure carried no query id,
139	/// which is today's process-wide wipe) and remembers the failure so later `Run`s of the query
140	/// are skipped. Returns the number of parked fragments dropped.
141	fn abandon_query<'ctx>(
142	    parked: &mut HashMap<u64, ParkedOutput<'ctx>>,
143	    parked_slots: &mut HashMap<SenderSlot, (u64, u64)>,
144	    poisoned: &mut HashMap<SenderSlot, String>,
145	    failed_queries: &mut FailedQueries,
146	    query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>,
147	    cause: &str,
148	) -> usize {
149	    if let Some(query_id) = query_id {
150	        failed_queries.insert(query_id, cause.to_string());
151	    }
152	    let doomed: HashSet<u64> = parked
153	        .iter()
154	        .filter(|(_, output)| query_id.is_none() || output.query_id == query_id)
155	        .map(|(park_id, _)| *park_id)
156	        .collect();
157	    if doomed.is_empty() {
158	        return 0;
159	    }
160	    // Same bound as today: only the most recent abandonment explains a missing slot.
161	    poisoned.clear();
162	    parked_slots.retain(|slot, (park_id, _)| {
163	        let keep = !doomed.contains(park_id);
164	        if !keep {
165	            poisoned.insert(*slot, cause.to_string());
166	        }
167	        keep
168	    });
169	    parked.retain(|park_id, _| !doomed.contains(park_id));
170	    doomed.len()
171	}
172	```
173	
174	`Err` arm becomes: log at `warn!` with `query_id`, `slots`, `error` ("discarding the failed
175	query's parked sender outputs"; the old wording stays for the `query_id: None` wipe), then
176	`abandon_query(..., request.label.query_id, &err)`. The `missing_slot` attribution
177	(`engine.rs:365-377`) is unchanged and still names the culprit.
178	
179	**(e) One new request.** `EngineRequest::AbandonQuery { query_id: FragmentInstanceId, cause: String }`
180	with **no respond channel**: its two callers must never wait behind a running fragment (the
181	cancel RPC runs on the BRPC current-thread runtime; the module doc at `engine.rs:16-21` records the
182	q02 wedge that motivates the rule). Handler: `abandon_query(..., Some(query_id), &cause)` plus the
183	same `warn!`. FIFO on the existing channel gives the ordering the design relies on: a `Run` queued
184	before the `AbandonQuery` executes and parks, then gets dropped; a `Run` queued after is skipped.
185	
186	### 2.2 `fragment_executor.rs`
187	
188	One trait method with a default:
189	
190	```rust
191	/// Best-effort, non-blocking: forget every parked output of `query_id` and refuse its later
192	/// runs. Called when the CN learns a query is dead (a fragment failed before or during its
193	/// run, or the FE cancelled it for a non-success reason). Unlike `drop_parked` this is a
194	/// sweep, not an exactly-once release, so an executor that parks nothing succeeds trivially.
195	fn abandon_query(&self, query_id: FragmentInstanceId, cause: String) -> Result<(), String> {
196	    let _ = (query_id, cause);
197	    Ok(())
198	}
199	```
200	
201	`SiriusEngine` implements it by sending `EngineRequest::AbandonQuery` and returning without
202	receiving (an `Err` only when the channel is closed, i.e. shutdown). `StubExecutor` and every test
203	executor inherit the default.
204	
205	### 2.3 `compute_node_service.rs`
206	
207	**(f) Dispatch-worker failure.** In `run_ready_fragment`'s `(Some(id), Some(query_id))` arm
208	(`compute_node_service.rs:877-897`), right after `self.results.fail_query(query_id, id, error)`:
209	
210	```rust
211	if let Err(err) = self.executor.abandon_query(query_id, error) {
212	    tracing::warn!(query_id = %query_id, error = %err, "could not abandon the failed query's parked output");
213	}
214	```
215	
216	This covers every CN-side pre-run failure that leaves inputs parked: translation
217	(`:1361-1362`, the q16 case), "exchange senders produced different output names" (`:1347`), the
218	sink validations (`:1066-1131`), a posted-drain failure (`:872`, `:160-163`). For an engine-side
219	`Err` it is redundant and idempotent.
220	
221	**(g) FE cancel for a non-success reason.** In `cancel_plan_fragment` (`:457-479`), keep the
222	existing `results.cancel(id, reason)` and add:
223	
224	```rust
225	use crate::proto::starrocks::PPlanFragmentCancelReason as CancelReason;
226	let reason_code = request
227	    .cancel_reason
228	    .and_then(|code| CancelReason::try_from(code).ok());
229	let query_finished = matches!(
230	    reason_code,
231	    Some(CancelReason::QueryFinished | CancelReason::LimitReach)
232	);
233	if !query_finished
234	    && let Some(query_id) = request.query_id.as_ref().map(FragmentInstanceId::from)
235	    && let Err(err) = self.core.executor.abandon_query(query_id, reason.clone())
236	{
237	    warn!(query_id = %query_id, error = %err, "could not abandon the cancelled query's parked output");
238	}
239	```
240	
241	(prost variant names per the generated enum, `target/.../out/starrocks.rs:3266`.) `QUERY_FINISHED`
242	and `LIMIT_REACH` are the two reasons the FE sends for a query whose rows it has; a missing or
243	unknown reason is treated as a failure (the existing cancel test at `:3414-3460` sends
244	`cancel_reason: None` with an "exceed big query cpu limit" message and `query_id: None`, so it
245	still reaches no engine call). The FE sends one cancel per instance, so a dead 11-fragment query
246	produces 11 `AbandonQuery` messages; each is a `HashMap` scan of a map that is empty after the first,
247	microseconds on the engine thread.
248	
249	Why the gate is safe rather than merely conservative: in this CN's single-batch result model
250	(`result_store.rs:245-283`) the FE can only be at `QUERY_FINISHED`/`LIMIT_REACH` after the result
251	fragment ran, and a receiver runs only after every sender it reads has parked or staged
252	(`local_exchange.rs:248-280`), so at that moment nothing of the query is parked on any CN; an
253	`AbandonQuery` would find nothing. Gating simply avoids the engine message on every passing query.
254	
255	### 2.4 Behaviour under the measured cases
256	
257	**q05 (engine-side failure on the worker).** 5774's `Run` returns `Err` at 13:05:24.627 ->
258	`abandon_query(Some(q05), ...)` drops the 2 parked slots (as today) and records q05. 5773's `Run`
259	(sent 5 ms later by the worker) is skipped without touching the GPU; so are 5777, 5776 and the
260	receiver 5775 (which today relayed 11 batches and parked 4.69 GB). `run_ready_fragment` logs each
261	skip and calls `fail_query` (no-op: first failure wins) and `abandon_query` (no-op: nothing
262	parked). The 11 FE cancels with reason 3 each queue an `AbandonQuery` that finds nothing. q06's
263	first fragment starts as soon as the worker reaches it: `QueryBegin allocated=0` instead of
264	4,690,817,280 bytes, and ~0.7 s earlier.
265	
266	**q16 (CN-side translation failure).** `ff87` and `ff86` park (6.6 GB). `ff85`'s translation fails
267	on the worker -> `fail_query` -> `abandon_query(Some(q16), "malformed plan ...")` -> the engine drops
268	both parked outputs and records q16. Pool returns to the pre-q16 baseline before q17 starts (today
269	+6.60 GB).
270	
271	**q21 -> q22.** `acc` (179 ms) and `acb` (3153 ms, 36.6 GB parked) are skipped; q22's first
272	fragment starts ~3.35 s earlier with `allocated=0` instead of 36.64 GB.
273	
274	**Sync dispatch mode (default, `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH` unset).** Senders run inside
275	their RPC threads and may already be queued on the engine channel ahead of the failing `Run`'s
276	return. Those already-queued `Run`s still execute and park (as today), then the `AbandonQuery`
277	sent by the FE cancel (or the worker's `Err` arm) drops what they parked. End state is clean; the
278	stolen time is bounded by fragments that were already queued at the failure, and every `Run` queued
279	after the `Err` is skipped by the failed-query memory. The campaign ran with async dispatch on
280	(`capture-cn.sh:12`), where the worker sends one `Run` at a time and nothing is queued ahead.
281	
282	**The 15 passing queries.** The `Run` arm does one `HashMap::get` on an empty map; the park stores
283	one `Option<FragmentInstanceId>`; the `Err` arm never runs; `run_ready_fragment`'s `Err` arm never
284	runs; every cancel carries reason 5 or 1 and takes the unchanged path. No engine message is added,
285	no ordering changes, no determinism change. The only visible difference is the cancel log line
286	gaining the decoded reason.
287	
288	### 2.5 Explicit non-goals (and why they are safe to leave)
289	
290	- **`LocalExchange` removal by query.** A dead query's `PendingReceiver` (a cloned
291	  `TExecPlanFragmentParams`, KB-scale host memory) and its `SenderSource::LocalParked` references
292	  stay in the rendezvous maps (`local_exchange.rs:87-95`). The GPU bytes they refer to are gone
293	  (dropped by query id), the receiver can never become ready (its failed sender never pushed), and
294	  if a leftover sender of the dead query did complete a set, the readied receiver's `Run` is
295	  skipped by the failed-query memory before it relays anything. Host-side KBs per failed query;
296	  not the measured GB-scale defect. Can be a follow-up with a `query_id` in `PendingReceiver`.
297	- **Aborting a fragment that is currently running.** The engine's single-flight lifecycle
298	  (`sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596`, per report B1) has no abort; that is fix 1's territory
299	  (fail-fast). This design only stops the next fragment.
300	- **`ResultStore` changes.** `cancel` keeps failing only `Waiting` entries; `fail_query` is not
301	  called from the cancel path (a `Pending` result must not be clobbered, `result_store.rs:490-504`).
302	
303	---
304	
305	## 3. Files to touch
306	
307	| file | change | approx. lines |

409	## 6. Risks
410	
411	| # | risk | why it is bounded |
412	|---|---|---|
413	| R1 | Sync dispatch mode: `Run`s already queued on the engine channel at failure time still execute and park | Bounded to fragments whose RPCs arrived before the failure (all of a query's RPCs arrive within ~100 ms of each other, B1); they are dropped by the `AbandonQuery` that follows; every later `Run` is skipped. Measured config (async on) has nothing queued ahead. No regression vs today. |
414	| R2 | Replacing the process-wide wipe removes the accidental "next failure cleans the last leak" safety net | Every path that can leave parked output unreachable now abandons the query explicitly: engine `Err` (d), worker pre-run `Err` (f), FE cancel for failures detected anywhere (g). Enumerated in section 2.4. The unlabelled case keeps the wipe. |
415	| R3 | Cancel gate misses a reason under which output is still parked | For `QUERY_FINISHED`/`LIMIT_REACH` nothing of the query is parked by construction (section 2.3); every other reason abandons. Regression-neutral: today nothing is dropped on any cancel. |
416	| R4 | `AbandonQuery` dropping a slot mid remote drain (4 CN) | Same as today's wipe: the next `export_packed_next` returns the poisoned cause, the drain fails, the transport's `drop_parked` warns (`nixl_transport.rs:409-418`). The FE already knows the query is dead. |
417	| R5 | Skipped result fragment reports "skipped ..." instead of the original error | `fail_query` keeps the first cause per query (`result_store.rs:174-179`) and the skip text embeds the original cause anyway. In sync mode a skipped sender's RPC returns INTERNAL_ERROR; the FE is already cancelling and ignores a second cancel (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1056-1058`). |
418	| R6 | `poisoned` growth | Cleared and refilled on every abandonment that drops something, exactly today's bound (`engine.rs:308-313`). |
419	| R7 | `FailedQueries` growth or a false skip | Capped at 1024 with FIFO eviction; ids are unique, so a false positive is impossible and a false negative needs a fragment pending across 1024 failures (> FE timeout). |
420	| R8 | Fire-and-forget send on a closed channel | `Err` returned and logged at warn; only at shutdown. |
421	| R9 | A `Run` interleaving with `AbandonQuery` | Impossible: both are handled by the single engine thread between requests; a running fragment lives on the stack, not in `parked`, and is abandoned when it parks (it is dropped by the later `AbandonQuery` or, if the failure came first, skipped). |
422	| R10 | Log noise: a skipped fragment still emits `fragment run started` / `fragment run failed` from `run_labeled` (`:1549-1578`) and an `error!` in `run_ready_fragment` | Cosmetic; the acceptance grep uses the `skipped` marker and `elapsed_ms`. A one-line `ResultStore::query_failure` check in `run_labeled` could silence it later; deliberately not in this change (second mechanism for the same predicate). |

1	# Fix 2, robust design: query-scoped teardown of parked output on the CN
2	
3	Angle: the design a senior engineer ships for the long run. Correct under cancellation and
4	concurrent queries, observable, configurable where it must be, with the failure modes written
5	down. Source tree read at `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` (branch
6	`perf/profile-sf1000`, 45dab3be); evidence at `scratchpad/perf/sf1000`. Every number is
7	**measured** (file named) or marked **inference**.
8	
9	## 0. Summary
10	
11	Today a query's parked sender output on a CN is released only by the receiver that consumes it.
12	When the query dies, three things go wrong (all measured on the 1-CN SF1000 sweep):
13	
14	1. The engine thread's `Err` path wipes **every** parked output process-wide
15	   (`engine.rs:291-316`), which is collateral damage for any concurrent query and does not even
16	   help the failing one on 1 CN (see 4.1).
17	2. The dead query's not-yet-run senders keep running and park output nobody will consume
18	   (`dispatch_worker` has no notion of a dead query, `compute_node_service.rs:380-390`):
19	   0-36.64 GB leaked per failure, 0.39-6.42 s of engine-thread time stolen from the next query.
20	3. `cancel_plan_fragment` touches only the result store (`compute_node_service.rs:449-476`), and
21	   a failure that never enters the engine (translation, q16) drops nothing.
22	
23	The design replaces the process-wide wipe with **one query-scoped teardown**,
24	`ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause)`, reachable from three triggers (a fragment
25	failure, an FE cancel, a TTL sweep) and acting on four subsystems (the engine's parked
26	registry, the dispatch path, the exchange rendezvous, the result store). Teardown is idempotent,
27	tolerates the transport's late `drop_parked`, refuses late `Run`s of the dead query at two gates,
28	logs one structured report per teardown, and has two knobs. It changes nothing on the hot path of
29	a healthy query beyond a hash lookup per fragment run.
30	
31	Predicted effect on the SF1000 1-CN sweep: the six post-failure leaks (4.69 / 8.83 / 31.56 /
32	+6.60 / 4.00 / 36.64 GB) become 0; the ~11.9 s of leftover-sender time (q05->q06 0.72,
33	q08->q09 1.04, q09->q10 0.39, q17->q18 6.42, q21->q22 3.35 s) disappears; q22 cold drops from
34	4110 ms to about 1.0-1.2 s; the 15 passing queries are unchanged (their QUERY_FINISHED cancels
35	tear down an empty registry).
36

170	### 2.5 What the FE sends
171	
172	`fe/fe-core/.../rpc/BackendServiceClient.java:192-209`: every cancel carries `finst_id`,
173	`cancel_reason`, `query_id` (always set) and `error_message` (non-empty only for
174	INTERNAL_ERROR). `qe/DefaultCoordinator.java:1003-1035`: on `getNext` failure ->
175	`dealStatusToTryRetry` -> `cancelInternal(INTERNAL_ERROR)`; on eos with >1 instance ->
176	`cancelInternal(QUERY_FINISHED)` or `LIMIT_REACH` (`:1028-1034`); `:1161-1177
177	cancelRemoteFragmentsAsync` calls `cancelFragmentInstance` for **every** deployed execution
178	(`FragmentInstanceExecState.java:383-415`: only DEPLOYING/EXECUTING instances are sent; the CN
179	accepts every dispatch immediately, so all are EXECUTING). Phased schedule uses
180	`ExecutionDAG.cancelQueryContext` (`:620-646`) with a dummy `finst_id (0,0)` per worker.
181	Proto: `gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto:464-482` (`LIMIT_REACH=1, USER_CANCEL=2,
182	INTERNAL_ERROR=3, TIMEOUT=4, QUERY_FINISHED=5`). The FE does not wait for the cancel reply
183	(`cancelPlanFragmentAsync` returns a `Future` that `cancelFragmentInstance` discards), but a slow
184	reply on the shared jprotobuf channel misattributes later replies (docstring at
185	`compute_node_service.rs:449-454`), so the cancel handler must keep returning immediately.
186	
187	Consequence for the design: on 1 CN, cancel arrives **after** the next leftover sender has
188	already started (0.25 ms late in q05), so Err-time bookkeeping on the CN is mandatory and cancel
189	is the second line; on N CNs, cancel is the only signal a *sender-side* CN gets that a query
190	failing on another CN is dead.

192	## 3. The design
193	
194	### 3.1 One entry point, three triggers, four subsystems
195	
196	```
197	trigger                     ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause)      subsystem action
198	------------------------    -------------------------------------------      --------------------------------
199	run_ready_fragment Err  ->  1. lifecycle.mark(query_id, cause)          ->  dispatch gate: later Runs skipped
200	process_fragment Err        2. executor.terminate_query(query_id,cause) ->  engine: mark + DropQuery (async)
201	cancel_plan_fragment    ->  3. exchanges.remove_query(query_id)         ->  rendezvous purged; staged leases
202	   (INTERNAL_ERROR,            + remove_receiver_instance(finst_id)         released via staging_release
203	    TIMEOUT, USER_CANCEL)   4. results.fail_query / nothing              ->  FE-polled ids fail (or untouched)
204	cancel_plan_fragment    ->  same, with cause = Finished (release-only)
205	   (QUERY_FINISHED,
206	    LIMIT_REACH)
207	TTL sweep (engine)      ->  engine-local drop_query + warn; CN lifecycle learns it on next touch
208	```
209	
210	`TerminationCause` is an enum, not a string: `Failed { fragment: FragmentInstanceId, error }`,
211	`Cancelled { reason: PPlanFragmentCancelReason, message: Option<String> }`,
212	`Finished { reason }` (QUERY_FINISHED / LIMIT_REACH), `Expired { idle: Duration }`. `Display`
213	renders the text that today's `missing_slot` (`engine.rs:369-377`) and the FE error carry.
214	
215	### 3.2 Engine thread: `ParkedRegistry`, a terminated set, two gates
216	
217	Extract the three maps at `engine.rs:267-275` into `experimental/starrocks/src/parked.rs`:
218	
219	```rust

221	
222	/// Everything the engine thread knows about parked sender output. Generic over the fragment
223	/// handle so the bookkeeping is unit-tested without a GPU (`F = ()` or a drop counter).
224	pub(crate) struct ParkedRegistry<F> {
225	    parked: HashMap<u64, ParkedOutput<F>>,
226	    slots: HashMap<SenderSlot, (u64, u64)>,

232	pub(crate) struct TornDown { pub query_id: Option<QueryId>, pub cause: Arc<TerminationCause>, pub at: Instant }

234	impl<F> ParkedRegistry<F> {
235	    pub fn park(&mut self, query_id: Option<QueryId>, label: FragmentLabel, slots: &[SenderSlot], fragment: F) -> Result<(), String>; // duplicate-slot refusal as today (engine.rs:703-707)
236	    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Result<(&mut F, u64 /*stream*/), SlotError>;  // SlotError::TornDown(cause) | Missing
237	    pub fn release(&mut self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Result<Release, String>; // Release::Freed | Release::Outstanding(n) | Release::AlreadyTornDown

246	Semantics that differ from today, each deliberate:
247	
248	- **`release` on a torn-down slot returns `Ok(Release::AlreadyTornDown)`** and removes the
249	  `torn_down` entry, so the transport's post-eos `drop_parked` (`nixl_transport.rs:790`) after a
250	  QUERY_FINISHED teardown, or its failure-path `drop_parked` (`:412`) after an INTERNAL_ERROR
251	  teardown, is not an error. A second release of a *live* slot stays a loud error (the
252	  exactly-once contract the transport tests pin, `compute_node_service.rs:2703-2757`).
253	- **`get_mut` (export / relay) on a torn-down slot returns `SlotError::TornDown(cause)`**,
254	  rendered as today's "sender output for {slot} was discarded when ... : {cause}" text so the
255	  q08-for-weeks diagnosis lesson (`engine.rs:270-275`) is kept, now naming the query and trigger.
256	- `torn_down` is bounded by time (`forget_torn_down_older_than(retain)`, default 600 s, run from
257	  the sweep) instead of "replace on next wipe".

379	### 3.5 Dispatch gates on the CN side
380	
381	- `run_ready_fragment` start: `if let Some(cause) = self.lifecycle.check(query_id) { info!(query_id, fragment_instance_id, %cause, "skipping fragment of a terminated query"); return Vec::new(); }`.
382	  This is what removes the leftover senders in async mode (they sit in the worker's inbox).
383	- `run_labeled` (`:1540-1581`), just before `self.executor.run(run)`: the same check, so a
384	  sender running inline in its RPC (default mode) is refused with
385	  `Err("fragment of terminated query ...")` instead of touching the engine. RPC threads already
386	  blocked in `engine_call` are caught by engine GATE 1.
387	- `process_fragment` for a **new** fragment of a terminated query (the FE's deploy of a late
388	  level racing its own cancel): refuse with the cause. The FE ignores the error (its
389	  `queryStatus` is already non-OK, `DefaultCoordinator.java:1056-1058`).

Result store untouched (a `Pending` entry the FE has not drained must not be failed). 406	### 3.7 Rendezvous: `LocalExchange::remove_query` / `remove_receiver_instance`
407	
408	`local_exchange.rs`: `PendingReceiver` gains `query_id: Option<QueryId>` (from
409	`params.params.query_id`, computed by the caller and passed to `register_receiver`);
410	`push_sender` gains a `query_id` argument (the sender's own, available at
411	`compute_node_service.rs:1193-1203`) recorded in `receiver_query: HashMap<FragmentInstanceId, QueryId>`.
412	Remote frames carry no query id on the wire (`internal_service.proto:812-827`), and none is
413	needed: the FE deploys receiver-first and waits for the level's replies before deploying senders
414	(`Deployer`, report P4), so the receiver is registered before its first frame; and every cancel
415	names the instance, so `remove_receiver_instance(finst_id)` purges any orphan `sources` entry
416	without a query mapping. `take_ready` keeps its removals; `remote_seq` is purged alongside.
417	
418	```rust
419	pub(crate) struct PurgedRendezvous { pub receivers: usize, pub sources: Vec<SenderSource> }
420	pub(crate) fn remove_query(&self, query_id: QueryId) -> PurgedRendezvous;
421	pub(crate) fn remove_receiver_instance(&self, id: FragmentInstanceId) -> Vec<SenderSource>;
422	```
423	
424	### 3.8 Sweep: the safety net for a silent FE
425	
426	A `std::thread` timer posts `EngineRequest::Sweep` every `min(ttl/4, 60 s)`; the engine thread
427	drops parked output whose query has had no touch (park, relay, export, frame) for
428	`SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` (default 1800; 0 disables) and warns once at `ttl/2`. The TTL must
429	exceed the FE's `query_timeout` (300 s default) by a wide margin because a receiver legitimately
430	waits for the slowest sender of its query. The sweep is the only path that frees memory when the
431	FE dies without cancelling, and it also prunes `torn_down`/`terminated` retention
432	(`SIRIUS_CN_TERMINATED_RETAIN_SECS`, default 600, bounded so a late deploy of a dead query is still
433	refused). Knobs go through `tunable.rs` (`Knob` with name/default/min/max, reject-not-clamp,
434	logged at bring-up; `tunable.rs:1-60`).
435

453	## 4. Behaviour under the measured cases
454	
455	### 4.1 The 1-CN SF1000 sweep, failure by failure
456	
457	The process-wide wipe was **not** the leak on 1 CN: at every wipe only the failing query's own
458	slots were parked (one query at a time), so today's `parked.clear()` and the new `drop_query`
459	free the same bytes. What changes is what happens next:
460	
461	| transition | today (measured) | with the design |
462	|---|---|---|
463	| q05 -> q06 | 5773/5777/5776/5775 run 13:05:24.632-25.355 (0.72 s), 5775 relays streams 1+4 and parks 4.69 GB that survives q06/q07 | engine `Err` at 13:05:24.626 marks q05 terminated on the engine thread; `run_ready_fragment` marks it on the CN and the worker's next pop (5773) is skipped with `skipping fragment of a terminated query`; 5777/5776/5775 likewise; the 11 cancels at .632 find q05 already torn down (idempotent). q06 starts at once; pool at q06 QueryBegin = 0.00 GB |
464	| q08 -> q09 | 6 leftovers 13:08:29.792-30.680 (1.04 s), 8.83 GB into q09 | skipped; 0 GB; q09's lineitem sender starts with a clean pool |
465	| q09 -> q10..q16 | 4 leftovers (0.39 s), 31.56 GB parked through 7 queries (21 runs); 47-178 ms reservation-gate blocks in q10/q12/q14 | skipped; 0 GB; the gate blocks in C3 lose their cause (**inference**: up to 0.18 s per q10/q12/q14 warm run recovered) |
466	| q16 (translation failure of receiver ff85) | senders ff86/ff87 parked 6.6 GB never dropped (no engine `Err`); +6.6 GB into q17 | `run_ready_fragment` `Err` -> `terminate_query(q16, Failed)` -> engine `DropQuery` frees ff86/ff87 within the same millisecond (engine idle) |
467	| q17 -> q18 | aca2 + aca1 (6.34 s scan) run after the failure, 4.0 GB into q18 | skipped: q18's timer starts 13:14:56.823 and its first fragment can start at ~.83 instead of 13:15:03.243 (6.42 s earlier) |
468	| q21 -> q22 | 2acc + 2acb (3.15 s, parks 36.64 GB) run after the failure; q22 cold 4110 ms, warm runs carry 36.64 GB | skipped; q22 cold = its own 0.755 s of fragments + FE head (~0.2 s, P4) + first-touch: predicted 1.0-1.2 s; warm 943 ms unchanged |
469	
470	Note the 0.25 ms race in q05: sender 5773 started **before** the first cancel ack. The design
471	does not depend on cancel for this; the CN marks the query at `run_ready_fragment`'s `Err`, which
472	executes on the dispatch worker *before* it pops 5773. In default (inline) mode the same senders
473	are RPC threads blocked in `engine_call`; engine GATE 1 refuses them because the engine thread
474	marked the query at its own `Err` before responding.

476	### 4.2 The 15 passing queries (1 CN and 4 CN)
477	
478	Per fragment run: one `HashMap` lookup in `run_ready_fragment`/`run_labeled`, one in engine
479	GATE 1, one in GATE 2, one `by_query` insert on park. Per query: 2-13 QUERY_FINISHED cancels
480	(`cn1-cnlog.txt cancels=`), each a `terminate_query(Finished)` that finds an empty registry
481	(every parked output was consumed before the result fragment could run, by construction of the
482	receiver-first rendezvous, B1) and logs at INFO. On 4 CNs a QUERY_FINISHED cancel can arrive on a
483	sender CN while the transport thread has transmitted eos but not yet called `drop_parked`
484	(`nixl_transport.rs:774-790`); `release` returns `AlreadyTornDown` and the drain reports success.
485	No plan, memory, or ordering change for these queries; warm medians should be within noise
486	(compare.py set unchanged).

488	### 4.3 Cases the campaign did not exercise
489	
490	- **User `KILL` mid-run** (USER_CANCEL while the engine is inside the query's fragment): cancel
491	  marks + posts `DropQuery`; the running fragment cannot be aborted (engine limitation, B3), but
492	  GATE 2 drops its output instead of parking, the CN never registers it, and every other fragment
493	  of the query is skipped. Memory returns as soon as the fragment ends.
494	- **Failure on another CN**: that CN's `run_ready_fragment` `Err` -> `fail_query` there; FE
495	  cancels every instance everywhere with INTERNAL_ERROR; this CN's parked output for the query
496	  (waiting on a drain, or already drained but the peer receiver died) is dropped by the cancel;
497	  an in-flight drain's next `export` fails with the teardown cause; staged remote frames for a
498	  receiver of the dead query on this CN are purged and their leases released (today they pin the
499	  arena forever, B6-adjacent).
500	- **FE dies, no cancel**: the sweep frees the output after `SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` and warns
501	  at half that; `parked_inventory` shows what is waiting.
502	- **Late deploy of a dead query** (FE level in flight when the failure happened): refused at
503	  `process_fragment` while the retention entry lives (600 s); after retention, it would register
504	  a receiver that never completes and be swept by the TTL.
505	
506	## 5. Failure modes of the design itself
507	
508	| # | scenario | what happens | why acceptable |
509	|---|---|---|---|
510	| F1 | QUERY_FINISHED cancel races the transport's post-eos `drop_parked` | `release` -> `AlreadyTornDown` (Ok) | test 7.5; without it a finished query's sender RPC would report an error |
511	| F2 | INTERNAL_ERROR cancel during an in-flight drain | next `export_packed_next` -> `Err(TornDown cause)`; drain fails; sender RPC / `fail_query` reports the teardown cause, not "no parked sender output" | the query is dead; the message names the culprit (the q08 lesson) |
512	| F3 | `terminate_query` for a query with a fragment mid-run on the engine | cannot abort; output dropped at GATE 2 when it ends | documented limitation; engine abort is fix-1/B3 territory |
513	| F4 | FE never sends cancel (crash) | TTL sweep frees after `SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` | default 1800 s >> FE query_timeout 300 s; knob |
514	| F5 | TTL too low for a legitimately long query (many-minute sender at SF10000) | its receiver fails with "sender output ... expired after N s" | loud, names the knob; warn at ttl/2 gives operators a signal first |
515	| F6 | Two failures of the same query (engine `Err` then CN `Err` then cancel) | `mark` keeps the first cause; later triggers log at DEBUG with `already_terminated=true` | idempotent by construction |
516	| F7 | Query id absent on the run (translate-only fixtures) | parked under `None`; only an `Err` of a `None` run drops the `None` bucket; never swept by query | preserves today's semantics for anonymous fragments |
517	| F8 | `DropQuery` posted while the engine is shutting down | `send_nowait` returns Err, logged; `Drop for SiriusEngine` drops the registry with the context (`engine.rs:359-361`) | nothing leaks past process exit |
518	| F9 | `staging_release` of a purged remote batch fails (arena gone) | warned, teardown continues | same tolerance as `engine.rs:470-476` |
519	| F10 | `terminated`/`torn_down`/`lifecycle` growth | bounded by retention (600 s) and by the sweep | one entry per query, pruned |
520	| F11 | A CN with async dispatch OFF and a sender RPC that failed at `route_destination` before running | `process_fragment` `Err` -> `terminate_query` | consistent: the FE fails the query on any RPC error |
521	| F12 | Knob `SIRIUS_CN_TEARDOWN_ON_CANCEL=0` | cancel reverts to `results.cancel`; Err-time and sweep paths still active | escape hatch only for the cancel contract |

676	## 10. Risks
677	
678	1. **Cancel contract drift.** The design assumes StarRocks sends QUERY_FINISHED only after the FE
679	   has every row (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1022-1035`). It does, and the CN's single-batch model
680	   means all parked output is consumed by then; the knob `SIRIUS_CN_TEARDOWN_ON_CANCEL` is the
681	   escape hatch. Mitigation: test 7.2.6/7.2.8 and the 4-CN smoke assertion `slots=0` on finished
682	   teardowns.
683	2. **Refusing a fragment the FE still expects.** `process_fragment` refusal of a late deploy of a
684	   terminated query returns an RPC error to an FE that has already failed the query -- harmless.
685	   If retention were shorter than the FE's deploy window the late fragment would register and be
686	   swept by the TTL instead; 600 s is far above any deploy.
687	3. **GATE 2 discards work.** Output of a fragment that finished after its query was terminated is
688	   dropped rather than parked; that is the intent, but a mis-marked query (a bug in a trigger)
689	   would lose a live query's output loudly ("terminated while running"). First-cause-wins and
690	   the cause text make such a bug diagnosable in one log line.
691	4. **TTL misconfiguration** (F5) can fail a long-running legitimate query; the default is 6x the
692	   FE query timeout and the warn-at-half gives a signal first. Set to 0 to disable in bring-up
693	   experiments.
694	5. **Engine backlog.** `DropQuery` is FIFO behind whatever the engine thread is doing; for a
695	   cancel during a 100 s fragment of the same query, the release happens when that fragment ends
696	   (F3). No new blocking anywhere.
697	6. **Interaction with fix 4(b) (spillable parked repositories).** If parked repositories get
698	   registered with the downgrade executor, dropping a `Fragment` must unregister them; flag to
699	   that design. Row counting already tolerates a spilled batch (`.ok()`).
700	7. **Behavioural change for the inline sender path**: a queued sender of a dead query now returns
701	   an RPC error instead of running; the FE already treats the query as failed, and
702	   `dispatched_receiver_failure_surfaces_through_fetch_data`-style tests cover the surfaced text.
