132	## 2. Design
133	
134	One CN PR, no engine C++ change, no FE patch, no proto change, no new environment knob.
135	
136	### 2.1 Principle
137	
138	*The engine holds parked state; the CN decides when a query is over.* The engine thread learns that a
139	query is over from two sources only: its own `Err` for a run of that query (immediately, on the same
140	thread, before it dequeues the next request), and an explicit `retire` request from the CN (for
141	pre-run failures and FE cancels). Every retirement is scoped to one query id, taken from the
142	`FragmentLabel` every run already carries (`fragment_executor.rs:57-63`; set from the FE params in
143	`compute_node_service.rs:1584-1589 fragment_label`).
144	
145	### 2.2 New module `experimental/starrocks/src/parked_registry.rs` (CI-compiled, no `sirius` dependency)
146	
147	The three loose maps and free functions in `engine.rs` (`parked`, `parked_slots`, `poisoned` at
148	:267-275; `missing_slot` :369-377; `export_next` :380-403; `release_slot` :408-425; the park block
149	:697-717) move into one generic struct so the bookkeeping is unit-testable without a GPU. `engine.rs` is
150	behind `#[cfg(feature = "sirius-engine")]` (`src/lib.rs:51-52`) and CI builds `--no-default-features`
151	(`Cargo.toml:44-51`), so today none of this logic runs in CI.
152	
153	```rust
154	/// One parked sender fragment and who still has a claim on it.
155	struct Parked<F> {
156	    fragment: F,
157	    /// The StarRocks query this output belongs to (`None` for unlabeled test runs).
158	    query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>,
159	    /// Destinations that have not yet released their stream.
160	    outstanding: usize,
161	}
162	
163	pub(crate) struct ParkedRegistry<F> {
164	    parked: HashMap<u64, Parked<F>>,
165	    slots: HashMap<SenderSlot, (u64, u64)>,
166	    /// Why a slot's output went away: filled by `retire`, replaced (never accumulated) on the
167	    /// next retirement. Same bound and same message contract as today's `poisoned`.
168	    poisoned: HashMap<SenderSlot, String>,
169	    next_id: u64,
170	}
171	
172	impl<F> ParkedRegistry<F> {
173	    /// Park once; each destination claims (id, stream i). Refuses a duplicate slot before
174	    /// inserting anything (today's engine.rs:697-717 contract).
175	    pub fn park(&mut self, query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>, outputs: &[SenderSlot], fragment: F)
176	        -> Result<(), String>;
177	    /// The parked fragment and stream a slot names (engine.rs:625-631 relay lookup, :386-392 export).
178	    pub fn claim(&mut self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Result<(&mut F, u64), String>;
179	    /// Read-only lookup used by the cardinality declaration (engine.rs:559-566).
180	    pub fn peek(&self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Option<(&F, u64)>;
181	    /// Exactly-once release of one destination's claim (engine.rs:408-425).
182	    pub fn release(&mut self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Result<(), String>;
183	    /// Drops every parked fragment of `query_id`, poisons its slots with `cause`, returns
184	    /// (fragments dropped, slots dropped). Idempotent: a second call returns (0, 0).
185	    pub fn retire(&mut self, query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>, cause: &str) -> (usize, usize);
186	    pub fn len(&self) -> usize;
187	}
188	
189	/// Queries this CN has declared over, so a run that was already queued for one of them is refused
190	/// instead of re-parking output nobody will consume. Bounded FIFO; a StarRocks query id is never
191	/// reused, so eviction only forgets an explanation, never a live query.
192	pub(crate) struct RetiredQueries {
193	    order: VecDeque<FragmentInstanceId>,
194	    causes: HashMap<FragmentInstanceId, String>,
195	}
196	impl RetiredQueries {
197	    pub const CAPACITY: usize = 64;
198	    pub fn mark(&mut self, query_id: FragmentInstanceId, cause: String);
199	    pub fn cause(&self, query_id: FragmentInstanceId) -> Option<&str>;

316	
317	```rust
318	let id = FragmentInstanceId::from(&request.finst_id);
319	let query_id = request.query_id.as_ref().map(FragmentInstanceId::from);
320	let reason_text = ...;                 // today's message, unchanged
321	self.core.results.cancel(id, reason_text.clone());            // unchanged
322	if let Some(query_id) = query_id {
323	    if !is_internal_cancel(request.cancel_reason) {           // LIMIT_REACH, QUERY_FINISHED are internal
324	        self.core.results.cancel_query(query_id, reason_text.clone());
325	    }
326	    self.core.release_staged(self.core.exchanges.retire_receiver(id)); // 2.5
327	    if let Err(err) = self.core.executor.retire_query(query_id, &reason_text) { warn!(...) }

331	  Reason codes come from `PPlanFragmentCancelReason` (`internal_service.proto:464-471`: LIMIT_REACH=1,

534	## 6. Risks and how the design bounds them
535	
536	1. **Refusing a run the FE still wants.** Only three events mark a query retired: the engine's own Err for
537	   that query, a recorded CN failure of that query, or an FE cancel for it. All are terminal on the FE side
538	   (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1048-1066`: a cancelled query cannot be cancelled twice and receives no new
539	   dispatches). `QUERY_FINISHED`/`LIMIT_REACH` retire parked state but record no failure, so a repeat
540	   `fetch_data` still sees EOS.
541	2. **Retiring a query whose remote drains are in flight** (same query, this CN is a sender): the transport
542	   thread's next `export_packed_next` fails with the retiring cause, its `drop_parked` warns (:412-418),
543	   and the RPC reports a failure the FE already knows. Today's wipe does the same to *every* query's drain.
544	3. **Refactor of the park/claim/release path.** Mechanical move of existing code into `ParkedRegistry`;
545	   covered by the two existing GPU tests and the new CI tests. Keep the `poisoned` replace-never-accumulate
546	   rule and its bound (engine.rs:308-313).
547	4. **Loss of the accidental sweep.** A parked output whose receiver never arrives and whose query never
548	   fails was, until now, freed by the next unrelated failure. With per-query scoping it stays until the
549	   FE's end-of-query cancel, which every multi-instance query receives (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1033`;
550	   measured `cancels=N` for all 15 passing queries). Single-instance queries get no cancel but also have
551	   no exchange and park nothing.
552	5. **Bounded memories.** `RetiredQueries` (64) and the exchange's `retired` FIFO (1024) are `const`s, not
553	   knobs; eviction forgets an explanation (a later drain gets the generic "no parked sender output") or, for
554	   the exchange, lets a very late frame re-create a source (today's behaviour). Query ids never recur.
555	6. **Inline-path recording is a behaviour change**: an inline sender failure now also fails the query's
556	   result instances reserved on this node with the real cause instead of the 600 s long-poll timeout. This
557	   is the documented reason `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH` is off by default (:284-288); the fix does not
558	   forward failures to other nodes, so that note stays true.
559	7. **Both dispatch modes must be tested** (the campaign ran with async on; the default is off); the CI
560	   tests run each relevant case in both modes.
561	8. **Fire-and-forget `RetireQuery`** loses its error return; the engine thread logs failures. The only
562	   failure mode is a closed channel (shutdown), when there is nothing left to drop.

3:#### B1 (confirmed). Receiver-first rendezvous plus one fragment at a time turn every exchange into a full GPU materialisation
5:**Source (verified).** `engine.rs:278-280`: `// One request at a time until the handle (and its sender) is dropped` `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()`; `run_fragment_inner` (engine.rs:486-720) does declare -> `build()` -> `relay_from` each parked sender -> `run()` -> park (engine.rs:697-716). `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 relay_from` throws unless the source fragment has run. `local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready` returns a receiver only when every expected sender is complete. The remote path is also park-then-export (`EngineRequest::ExportNext`, engine.rs:91-95). Inside the engine, `Fragment::build()` opens a `StandaloneQueryScope` that takes the single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` (`sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596`) until `run()` finishes, so two fragments cannot be in flight on one context even if the CN asked (source skeptic; this makes "run sender and receiver concurrently" engine work, not CN work).
7:**Measured, q05 timeline.** All 11 `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs arrived 13:03:43.358-43.462 (cn1/cluster.log 4142-4202). Fragments ran strictly sequentially: nation 6 ms, region 9 ms, then the lineitem sender 5774 started 13:03:43.434 with `allocated=2304 bytes` (engine-cn0.log:49203, an empty pool) and parked 39 batches x 2.668 GB = 104.06 GB by +1.315 s (Quent data_batch Stationary events: 26.7 GB at +0.32 s, 66.7 GB at +0.88 s); first OOM at +1.361 s (engine-cn0.log:49221 `requested 748875880 bytes ... global usage 107374182400 bytes (102400.00 MB), peak allocated 3376381184, reservation 3318948864`). The supplier/customer/orders fragments started only after the failure at 13:05:24.632+ (cluster.log 6072-6305); the receiver of streams 7 and 9 never started (Quent shows 7 of 11 fragments). Receiver 5775 later ran in 73 ms and its output sat parked for 184.5 s until q08's failure wipe (cn1-quent.txt wall=184.502 s, Comp=0.128 s).
9:**Measured, passing queries show the same shape under the cap.** cn1 q07.r0: all 7 senders finished before the join fragment started (cluster.log 6807-7005); 59.47 GB of lineitem plus 18.38 GB of orders were parked (79.1 GB, 74% of the pool) with dwell up to 2.76 s. cn4 q07.r1: every `fragment run finished` precedes its first `transmitted batches via nixl`. Per-fragment run sums vs span (MFS-4): cn1 q02.r1 13 fragments sum 977 ms, span 1067 ms, gaps 90 ms (8%); cn4 q02.r1 cn0 sum 748 ms, span 1081 ms, gaps 333 ms (31%), the largest before receivers waiting for the other CNs' senders. The 4-slot executor idles during the many 1-task fragments (cn1 q02.r1: 133 tasks, Comp 2.9 s in a 1.06 s span = 2.7 of 4 slots busy).
19:**Source (verified).** `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`: `// Repositories escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup so sender output outlives this fragment.` `_output_repos[id] = std::make_shared<cucascade::shared_data_repository>()` (and `_input_repos` likewise). The only registration path into a per-query manager is `repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68-71 add_new_repository` (inter-pipeline ports). `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232` TIER 1 iterates `_data_repo_registry.get_all()` managers only; `:294-300` TIER 2 the pipeline task queue (queued GPU_SCAN tasks hold no input batches). The warning at `:357-363` fires whenever no DISK tier exists and the request is unsatisfied, regardless of whether any candidate existed. `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066 output_row_count` throws on a non-GPU-resident parked batch (the CN swallows it with `.ok()` and plans blind, engine.rs:564, 582-585); `:822-825 export_packed` throws too, which would fail the 4-CN path on a spilled batch.
25:**Proposed.** Register the streaming sink's output repositories and the receiver's input repositories with a process-level registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, including the running fragment's own sink (otherwise q05/q08/q09 still die). Make `Fragment::output_row_count` read a row count from host metadata and `export_packed` accept HOST-tier batches (the local relay already upgrades HOST -> GPU in `lock_or_prepare_batch`). Correct the warning to distinguish "no convertible candidates" from "no disk tier". Note the newest-first fairness policy at `downgrade_executor.cpp:204-216`; the candidate that matters here is the newest fragment's own output. Confidence high on the mechanism, medium that spill is worth doing before P1/B1.
27:#### B3 (confirmed). The reschedule loop has no feasibility check: 179 stuck scan tasks x 100 retries x 50 ms, re-reading the split each time, while nothing can free memory
42:Offsets are from the client start in `cn1/runs/runs.csv` (q05 13:03:43.185); B1's "+1.361 s" for q05 is the same first OOM (13:03:44.795) measured from the lineitem sender's start (13:03:43.434). Every original task reaches exactly retry 100; the retry chain of q05 task 2567 is byte-identical on all 101 attempts (requested 748,875,880 B, peak 3,376,381,184 B; the retry floor raised the request from 5.80 to 6.64 GB while the grant stayed at 3.08-3.32 GB = cap minus parked bytes). Quent q05 fragment 5774: `GPU_SCAN n=2543 Computing sum 229.5 s` (about half of it is the 50 ms sleep, which Quent counts inside Computing), `Queued 2228.6 s`, `Reserving 99.9 s`, for 40 useful batches that took 1.3 s. The storm is paced by the single manager thread blocking in `make_reservation` (Reserving sum equals the retry window: q05 99.9 s of 101.2), not by the sleeps. Exactly one successful task finalised after the first OOM in each of the six windows. The six failures consumed 774.9 s of the 910.3 s 1-CN sweep (85%). Log volume: 89,580 of 152,097 engine-log lines are the five per-retry lines. `SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS` cannot detect the storm because each reschedule creates and destroys a task, advancing the watchdog fingerprint (`sirius_engine.cpp:113-125`).
44:**Proposed.** At the reservation gate (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263`) abort the query when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry_reservation_floor > reservation->size()` (all three are local there), or in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and `global usage == usage_limit` and no successful completion happened since this task's previous attempt (`_tasks_executed` at `:310` is success-only). Keep the 100-retry budget for the contention case, which arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the reservation gate. Message the engine can emit: "104 GB parked by this fragment's sink, 3.1 GB grantable < 6.6 GB floor, downgrade freed 0 bytes". Effect: each failure dies in ~3 s (q18 ~10 s because its own senders run first). Confidence high; this is a robustness finding, no wrong result is produced.
46:#### B4 (disputed: mechanism confirmed, causal claim refuted). Fragments of a failed query keep running and park output nobody consumes; the leak is 0-38 GB per failure but decided no pass/fail here
48:**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:449-476 cancel_plan_fragment` only calls `results.cancel()`; its log line reads `acknowledging cancel_plan_fragment (best-effort: no engine-side abort yet)` (:468) and the docstring says teardown "is a separate work item". `engine.rs:291-316` drops parked outputs only when `run_fragment` returns `Err`, and then wipes every slot process-wide. `ResultStore.query_failures` (result_store.rs:98) is recorded but never consulted on the sender path. A translator failure before the run (q16) drops the `LocalParked` slots without `drop_parked`.
50:**Measured** (engine-cn0.log `[gpu_pool] allocated` at fragment boundaries, agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt `base@start`): after q05 4.69 GB carried through q06/q07; after q08 8.83 GB into q09; after q09 31.56 GB through q10..q16 (seven queries); +6.6 GB from q16's parked partsupp scan -> 38.16 GB at q17's start; after q17 4.0 GB into q18; after q18 0; after q21 36.64 GB into q22 (q22 cold 4110 ms vs 943 warm). cluster.log shows the dead query's queued senders starting after `fragment run failed` (q05: 5773, 5777, 5776, 5775 at 13:05:24.632+, the first 0.25 ms before the FE's first cancel ack). Engine-thread time stolen from the next query: q17 -> q18 6.42 s, q21 -> q22 ~3.35 s, q08 -> q09 1.04 s.
52:**Objection (both skeptics).** "Directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB of its own data parked" is arithmetically false: q17's F00 lineitem projection is ~120-122 GB (46 tasks x 2.65 GB; standalone `GPU_SCAN(3) n=46 in=122.25 GB`), above the 107.37 GB cap, so it fails with zero leak; the leak only moved the death from ~40 to 25 parked batches. Every passing query that ran under a leak passed with `oom_resched=0` (q06/q07 under 4.69 GB, q10-q15 under 31.6-38.2 GB, q22 under 36.6 GB). No pass/fail in this campaign was decided by the leak. The order-dependence risk is real but inferred: q07's own parked footprint is 79.17 GB; under the 38.16 GB leak it would need ~117 GB and would have failed had it run between q09 and q17. The cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of the pool occupied (the reservation-gate blocks in C3 need that leak to occur).
54:**Proposed (small, high confidence as hygiene).** Store `query_id` with each `ParkedOutput`; on `Err` drop only that query's slots; keep a failed-query set on the engine thread and skip its pending `Run`s (Err-time bookkeeping, since cancel arrives after the next sender already started); make `cancel_plan_fragment` drop the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeue its fragments (needs a `LocalExchange` removal by query; today removals happen only in `take_ready`, local_exchange.rs:284-308); in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm `drop_parked` the slots already in hand when translation fails.
62:**Corrections to the proposals.** More transport threads (b) or a non-joining dispatch worker (c) cannot deliver the claimed saving on their own: packs and fragment `Run`s share the one engine thread, so packs still serialise, and a fragment started during a drain competes with `ExportNext` in the same FIFO; the upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the ~16% non-pack part (~45 ms per CN on q03). Packing during execution into staging leases (a, first variant) would need ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured, and exhaustion is a hard failure (B6). The impact sentence "small fragments could have overlapped the lineitem scan" is wrong for the current engine (one fragment at a time, B1); only the drain itself, ~0.25-0.28 s of q03's 1.42 s span, is recoverable.
64:**Proposed.** Move `export_packed` off the engine thread (needs `ParkedOutput`/`Fragment` reachable from another thread; the parked map lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272) and make it faster: try a larger `kPackChunkBytes` or a single `cudf::pack` for GPU-resident batches (the receiver-side copy of the same bytes is 30x faster, so the 8 MiB chunking is the suspect; inference, medium confidence). Then (b)/(c) add value. Expected gain 0.15-0.3 s per shuffle stage at 4 CNs for q03/q10/q12 (inference). Confidence high on the mechanism.
94:## 4. What to do first
100:| 1 | Fail fast in the OOM reschedule loop when the downgrade freed 0 bytes, usage == limit and the retry floor exceeds the grantable reservation (B3) | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263` (reservation gate) or `:330-420` (reschedule path) | the six failures die in ~3 s instead of 54-232 s (measured: 775 s of the 910 s sweep); the error names the real cause | keep the 100-retry budget for the cross-GPU contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory`, not the gate); needs `freed`/`global_usage` plumbed into the reschedule path if implemented there | high |
101:| 2 | Per-query parked-output bookkeeping: drop only the failed query's slots, skip its pending `Run`s, drop slots on cancel and on pre-run translation failure (B4) | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs:291-316, ~626-643`; `compute_node_service.rs:449-476, 864-905, 1325-1400`; `local_exchange.rs` | removes the 0-38 GB leaks (measured) and 0.4-6.4 s of stolen engine time per failure; restores order-independence of results | Err-time bookkeeping is required (cancel arrives after the next sender started) | high |
103:| 4 | Make the six queries runnable on 1 CN: either (a) same-node fragment fusion before translation, or (b) parked repositories visible to the downgrade sweep + HOST-tier `output_row_count`/`export_packed` (P1, B1, B2) | (a) `compute_node_service.rs process_fragment` / `local_exchange.rs register_receiver` at the `TPlan` level; (b) `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`, `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:822-825, 1062-1066` | (a) reproduces the standalone plan that passes all six at 2.7-6.4 s; (b) five of six would plausibly pass slowly (q09 marginal at ~253 GB vs 279 GB GPU+HOST) | (a) substantial; 1-CN only; q21 also needs #5; (b) medium effort; spill throughput unknown | medium |

265:### PR reviewability
266-
267-PRs sometimes stall for weeks after a reviewer is assigned, simply because the PR wasn't actually
268-ready to review the moment CODEOWNERS pinged someone. Before marking a PR ready for review, please
269-do the following:
270-
271-1. **State the motivation, not just the mechanics.** Link the originating issue (`Closes #NNN` /
272-   `Refs #NNN`) if one exists; if there isn't one, the description itself should explain *why* the
273-   change is needed, not just summarize the diff.
274-2. **Scope the PR to one reviewable sitting.** If a reviewer can't get through it start-to-finish
275-   without losing context, either split it (see [Stacked PRs](#stacked-prs)) or explicitly justify
276-   in the description why it can't be split.
277-3. **Make the description self-sufficient.** A reviewer should be able to start reviewing without
278-   needing to ask what changed or why — cover what changed, why, how it was verified, and anything
279-   non-obvious (e.g. "intentionally doesn't handle X, tracked in #NNN").
280-4. **Open as a draft until 1-3 are actually true**, then convert to "Ready for review" — that's
281-   the point CODEOWNERS review requests and author auto-assignment (`auto-assign.yml`) trigger, so
282-   converting early means a reviewer gets pinged before there's anything reviewable yet.
283-
284-### Commit and title convention
285-
286-Sirius squash-merges PRs, the PR titles become the commit message on merge. Commits and PR titles follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format for readability.
287-
288-Example of Conventional Commits:
289-```
290-<type>[optional scope]: <description>
291-
292-[optional body]
293-
294-[optional footer(s)]
295-```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run bench-kit TPC-H queries against the FE on 9030 with a /* marker */ so the FE audit log ties QueryId to (query, run).
# usage: run-queries.sh <tag> <tpch_data> <out_dir> <timeout_s> <runs_after_warmup> q01 q02 ...
# writes <out_dir>/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc) and <out_dir>/<q>.r<i>.out (mysql --batch)
TAG=$1; DATA=$2; OUT=$3; TO=$4; RUNS=$5; shift 5
QD=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf/experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries
mkdir -p $OUT; echo "query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc" > $OUT/runs.csv
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
for q in "$@"; do
  sql=$(sed "s#__TPCH_DATA__#$DATA#g" $QD/$q.sql)
  for i in $(seq 0 $RUNS); do
    phase=warm; [ $i = 0 ] && phase=cold
    start=$(date -u +%FT%T.%3N); t0=$(date +%s%N)
    if timeout $TO $M -e "/* $TAG $q r$i */ $sql" > $OUT/$q.r$i.out 2> $OUT/$q.r$i.err; then st=pass; else st=fail; rc=$?; fi
    ms=$(( ($(date +%s%N) - t0) / 1000000 )); rows=$(( $(wc -l < $OUT/$q.r$i.out) - 1 )); [ $rows -lt 0 ] && rows=0
    [ $st = fail ] && [ $ms -ge $((TO*1000 - 500)) ] && st=timeout
    echo "$q,$i,$phase,$st,$ms,$rows,$start" >> $OUT/runs.csv
    echo "$q r$i $phase $st ${ms}ms rows=$rows $( [ $st != pass ] && head -c 160 $OUT/$q.r$i.err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [ $st != pass ] && break   # a failing run skips the rest of that query (bench.sh semantics)
  done
done

content.thinking: I've confirmed all the source details across the three designs, FE behavior, and delivery tooling line up as expected. I'm ready to proceed with scoring.

scores.notes: Removes every measured 1-CN leak (4.69/8.83/31.56/+6.60/4.00/36.64 GB, headroom.txt base@start) and the 11.9 s of leftover-fragment time: engine-side Err marks the query on the engine thread before the next dequeue, so in the campaign's async mode (capture-cn.sh:12) 5773/5777/5776/5775 and q21's acb are skipped; the worker Err arm at compute_node_service.rs:877-897 covers q16's translation failure; reason-gated cancel (proto :464-471, generated starrocks.rs:3266-3271) keeps the 15 passing queries on an unchanged path (cancels are reason 5/1 only, cn1-cnlog.txt). Two as-written defects cost points. (1) The engine skip is placed at the Run dequeue (engine.rs:282-318) BEFORE run_fragment, so a skipped Run's remote_inputs never reach the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478: on 4 CNs a dead query's receiver with staged batches in hand leaks its staging-arena leases for the process lifetime, which is a regression against today (today the leftover receiver runs and the push loop releases them). Fix is a placement change: put the check as the first statement inside run_fragment, exactly where the upstream design puts it. (2) No CN-side gate: in async mode a dead query's sender still goes through execute_ready_fragment -> translate -> run_labeled and emits 'fragment run started'/'fragment run failed' before the engine refuses it (the design's R9/R10), so the plan's literal acceptance line 'no fragment run started for a dead query' does not hold; the design substitutes elapsed_ms<=5 + a 'skipped' marker. The design also understates itself in R1/2.4: after an engine-side Err the engine-local FailedQueries is set before the next dequeue, so queued Runs in sync mode ARE skipped; only CN-side failures and cancels have the FIFO window. Core retain logic lives in cfg-gated engine.rs, so CI never runs it (lib.rs:51-52; experimental.yml:79); only the two GPU tests do. ~110 code + ~240 test lines, three files, one fork PR, half a day.

Covers everything measured plus the multi-CN cancel cleanup (rendezvous purge + staged-lease release), idempotent late drop_parked, TTL sweep, retention, telemetry, three knobs. Largest blast radius: every QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH cancel of a passing query now runs terminate_query (engine DropQuery message per instance, 2-13 per query per cn1-cnlog.txt cancels=, exchanges.remove_query, remove_receiver_instance), release() semantics change (AlreadyTornDown is Ok, weakening the exactly-once contract the transport tests pin at compute_node_service.rs:2703-2757), GATE 2 discards a running fragment's output if the query was marked mid-run (a mis-mark loses live output), the TTL default (1800 s) can fail a legitimately long query, push_sender/register_receiver signatures change, and two terminated maps (engine + ServiceCore) must stay in sync. GATE 1 sits at the Run dequeue and therefore has the same lease-sweep bypass as the surgical skip, mitigated only by the CN-side gate and remove_query's lease release (a cancel racing an in-flight dispatch still leaks). PR 3 (sweep/knobs/docs) is scope beyond the measured problem: the FE already cancels every multi-instance query (DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1034, measured cancels=N), so the accidental-sweep loss is covered without a timer. Three stacked fork PRs, 3.5-4 engineer-days; the stack's PR 2 alone touches compute_node_service.rs, local_exchange.rs and result_store.rs and is borderline for one sitting. Test plan is the best of the three (CI-tested registry, component tests in both dispatch modes, 4-CN smoke) and its acceptance greps match the plan literally.

Covers the measured leaks and stolen time, q16, the inline-path failure recording, staged-lease release on refusal and on translation failure, cancel teardown (parked + rendezvous + late-frame refusal), with the dead-query check correctly placed INSIDE run_fragment so the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 still runs. Extracting ParkedRegistry<F> into a non-gated module makes the park/claim/release/retire bookkeeping CI-testable for the first time (engine.rs is never compiled in CI); RetiredQueries is an Arc<Mutex> marked by both the engine Err arm and SiriusEngine::retire_query, so already-queued Runs are refused in both dispatch modes. Correctness risk is moderate-low: the cancel path now acts on ALL reasons including QUERY_FINISHED (N fire-and-forget sends + N retire_receiver inserts per passing query; empty retires), and the inline RPC error path now records fail_query (a behaviour change the design owns). The theoretical QUERY_FINISHED-vs-post-eos drop_parked race is practically closed by FIFO ordering (DropParked is enqueued right after rpc_transmit returns at nixl_transport.rs:790, long before an FE round trip) and would only produce a spurious drain error on a finished query. Bounded consts (64/1024), no knobs. Roughly 400 non-test + 500 test lines across 6 source files + a new module, one PR in two commits (commit 2 can be stacked); ~2 engineer-days + one GPU session. The refactor of the relay/export/release path is mechanical but is what pushes it past a quick review. Acceptance greps ('skipping fragment of a retired query', no 'fragment run started' after 'fragment run failed', QueryBegin allocated within 1 MB of baseline) match the plan literally; the 4-CN arm with q16 as the deliberate failure is runnable with capture-cn.sh 4.

input.reasoning: Delivery-side judgement. All three designs rest on the same verified mechanisms (engine.rs:267-275/282-318/697-717 wipe and park; compute_node_service.rs:380-390 worker, :864-911 Err arm with fail_query at :896, :457-479 cancel stub, :1358-1362 translate-before-slots; result_store.rs query_failures consulted only in reserve :127; local_exchange.rs take_ready :248-313 as the only removal; FE per-instance cancels with query_id at BackendServiceClient.java:192-206 and QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH only after eos at DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1034) and the same measured evidence (headroom.txt base@start; cluster.log 6050-6305 for q05, 16585-16610 for q16; cn1-cnlog.txt cancels=N; refute-oom5/notes.md stolen time). B4 established this fix is hygiene and order-independence, not a pass/fail flip, so the value ceiling is fixed and the deciding criteria are blast radius, PR size, and how fast the acceptance arm runs. The surgical design gets the whole measured 1-CN effect in ~110 code lines in three files with a provably unchanged path for the 15 passing queries (no cancel-path change for reasons 5/1, one HashMap::get per Run), can be implemented in half a day in the already-built fix-parked-bookkeeping worktree (engine + CN built 15:51 today, GPUs idle now), and its smoke arm (q05 q06 q16 q17 q21 q22) runs in ~7 minutes with existing tooling (capture-cn.sh, run-queries.sh, headroom.txt, cnlog_extract.py). It is the '80% for 20%' version and the answer to whether a smaller version suffices is yes. It is not mergeable exactly as written: its Run-dequeue skip bypasses the remote-lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 (a 4-CN staging-arena leak that today does not exist, because the leftover receiver runs and releases its leases), and without a CN-side gate the dead query's senders still translate and log 'fragment run started' before the engine refuses them, so the plan's literal acceptance wording fails. Both are fixed by lifting two small pieces from the upstream design (~20 lines): the check inside run_fragment, and refuse_if_retired at the top of run_ready_fragment reading the query_failures record that fail_query already writes, releasing SenderSource::Remote staged batches from ready.inputs. The upstream design is the best engineering of the three (CI-testable registry, correct check placement, both dispatch modes, cancel teardown closing the multi-CN staged-lease leak) and would be the right shape for an eventual dev-bound CN PR, but it is 3-4x the diff and ~2 days, and its extra coverage (rendezvous purge, late-frame refusal, inline-path recording) addresses paths the campaign did not measure; it fits better as the follow-up PR once fix 2's SF1000 arm is green. The robust design over-delivers against the measured problem (TTL sweep and three knobs for a case the FE's measured cancels=N already covers), changes the release contract and the cancel path for every passing query, spans three PRs and ~4 days, and its GATE 1 has the same lease-sweep bypass. Landing order, on which all three agree and which I endorse: land fix 2 before fix 1's SF1000 time-to-fail arm, because the 0.7-6.4 s of leftover-fragment time (q17->q18 6.42 s) would otherwise confound that measurement; no proto, FE, or engine C++ change, so no other dependency. Acceptance on this box: smoke ~7 min, full 22-query arm ~16 min today (~4 min once fix 1 lands); avoid the 02:00-03:50 UTC nightly window.
disqualifiers: None of the three is disqualified outright; each works for the measured 1-CN failure. Two as-written defects must be corrected before merge: (a) surgical: the engine-side skip at the Run dequeue (engine.rs:282-318) bypasses run_fragment's remote-lease sweep (engine.rs:462-478), so on 4 CNs a refused Run that carries remote_inputs leaks its staging-arena leases for the process lifetime, a regression against today; move the check inside run_fragment (the upstream design's placement). (b) robust: GATE 1 at the Run dequeue has the same bypass; its CN-side gate and remove_query lease release cover most of it but a cancel racing an in-flight dispatch still leaks; same fix. The upstream design has no as-written defect; its only behaviour change worth a second look is acting on QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH cancels for every passing query (N fire-and-forget sends and retire_receiver inserts), which is harmless by construction but is a change on the hot path the surgical gate avoids.
input.merge_suggestions: Into the surgical design, mandatory: (1) from upstream, place the dead-query check as the first statement inside run_fragment (engine.rs:430-481) rather than at the dequeue, so the lease sweep at :462-478 runs for a refused Run; (2) from upstream, add ServiceCore::refuse_if_retired at the top of run_ready_fragment (:864) consulting a new ResultStore::failure_of(query_id) accessor over the query_failures map that fail_query already writes (result_store.rs:96-98, :163-200), logging 'skipping fragment of a retired query' and releasing SenderSource::Remote staged batches in ready.inputs via executor.staging_release (len > 0), so no 'fragment run started' is emitted for a dead query and the plan's acceptance grep holds literally; add the skips= column to cnlog_extract.py as upstream proposes. Recommended, not blocking: (3) from upstream, make the abandon/retain logic generic over the fragment type and host it in a small non-feature-gated module so the retain-only-this-query logic gets a CI test (engine.rs is never compiled in CI, experimental.yml:76-79); the full ParkedRegistry refactor can wait. (4) from upstream, release Remote staged leases in run_ready_fragment's Err arm for the translation-failure case at 4 CNs (today's ready.inputs are dropped on the floor at :1361-1362). Defer to a follow-up PR (upstream's commit 2 as a stacked PR): cancel_plan_fragment purging LocalExchange state by receiver instance with staged-lease release and late-frame refusal (closes the multi-CN arena leak the campaign did not measure), and the inline-path fail_query recording. Take from robust only if the 4-CN smoke ever shows a drop_parked-after-teardown error: the idempotent AlreadyTornDown release.
